picks.title: Closing the Gap Between Policy and Practice
picks.rationale: Primary-source policy change: Runway's moderation now allows genre violence (sword fights, shootouts, horror) but still blocks real harm, and explains how to flag false blocks. This changes what filmmakers can generate tomorrow.
picks.excerpt: Runway’s moderation now allows sword fights, shootouts and horror while blocking real harm. What changed, where limits remain and how to flag mistakes.

picks.title: We Tested Kling 4.0 Against Seedance 2.5, and It’s Not Close
picks.rationale: First hands-on test of the new Kling 4.0 against Seedance 2.5 on cinematic shots, from a whitelisted AI-filmmaking channel. Useful for choosing a video model.
picks.excerpt: Curious Refuge puts Kuaishou's new Kling 4.0 video model head-to-head with ByteDance's Seedance 2.5 on cinematic shots to test claims that Kling now leads AI filmmaking quality.

picks.title: Netflix Officially Bans AI From Blue Eye Samurai Production
picks.rationale: A concrete production-level decision: Netflix commits that its flagship animated series will never use generative AI. A clear signal for how studios set AI rules show by show.
picks.excerpt: Fans of Netflix's French-produced samurai epic can breathe easy -- generative AI is not and never will be utilized by the series' production team.

picks.title: Even Martin Scorsese uses AI for storyboards. Can the art survive?
picks.rationale: Reported feature on storyboard artists, the first pre-production craft AI is displacing, with the Scorsese example. A new angle not covered in the 30-day history.
picks.excerpt: As Hollywood begins to adopt the technology, the professionals in most direct jeopardy are the illustrators mapping out directors’ first visions. They sketch out what could be lost

picks.title: CHILEMONOS 2027 Opens Free Oscar-Qualifying Animation Entries With New AI Restrictions
picks.rationale: New eligibility rule at an Oscar-qualifying festival: works where AI replaces the animator's creative contribution are ineligible. Directly affects what animators can submit.
picks.excerpt: Oscar-qualifying Chilean animation festival CHILEMONOS opens 2027 submissions with rules that prohibit AI in submitted works, making AI-generated animation that replaces an animator's creative contribution grounds for ineligibility — another festival following Manchester's gen-AI ban.

dedup.note: Pool had 22 items. Dropped as duplicates or follow-ups: Yonhap AKR20261114030800073 (Japan AI likeness rules) already ran in politics on 11-15 per the cross-section brief. THR Camerimage founder interview is commentary on the Camerimage/AI story already published 11-09. No Film School 'Premiere audio tools' covers the same Enhance Audio/stem-separation features as the 10-20 ProVideo Coalition card. Not picked: Adgully Mahabharat S2 trailer (related to the 10-26 Variety Mahabharat card; a trailer drop is weak), 3DVF RUS-T (reads as a Reallusion promo), LA Times Sean Astin and Deadline Pedro Pascal (profile/commentary; SAG-AFTRA AI stance already covered 11-13), Alvin & Chipmunks backlash, TOI Jungle Book voice casting, and Korean items (Daum AI short drama, Aria Studio CES award, AnAI DynEx, Dexter media art, MTN Raphael interview, Ajunews overview, K-EnterTech IP piece), all lower on actionability. History-match notes: CHILEMONOS is a different festival and a new rule, not the Manchester policy (11-14). Kling 4.0 vs Seedance is a test of a new Kling model, not the Seedance 2.5 launch (10-29) or 2.5 Flash (11-14). The Runway moderation-policy post is a concrete policy change, distinct from the 10-28 safety summit talk. Cross-section: published_urls.json is URL-keyed and this agent has no grep tool. All 5 pick URLs are new to the movies 30-day history, but an exact all-section grep for the URLs and for 'Kling 4.0' was not run. The orchestrator should verify before roll.
